_readme: Resume state for the newsletter harvest (tools/upkeep-routine.md step 2).

Each source resolves its next issue for `harvest prep` by `url_pattern` (numbered URLs) or, for slug-titled sources, by `feed` + `issue_label` (RSS, number read off the page) or `archive_slug` (number embedded in the archive's slugs) — tools/harvest-lib.mjs discoverIssues.
Read this BEFORE a harvest pass; update `last_processed`/`count`/`updated` and COMMIT it after.
This file lives in the repo (not session memory) precisely so a CLOUD agent can clone, resume, and open a PR.
`react-brain lint` cross-checks each `count` against encyclopedia.yaml sources_digested — they must match.
Narrative harvest history (what each pass changed, process learnings) lives in tools/harvest-log/LEDGER.md — in-repo since 2026-08-07.

this-week-in-react.name: This Week in React
this-week-in-react.notes: issue pages fetch directly at /newsletter/{n} — BUT A 200 IS NOT PROOF OF PUBLICATION: cross-check the ARCHIVE listing at /newsletter or reject titles ending in ': ...' before treating an issue as live. That rule EARNED ITS KEEP AGAIN on 2026-09-21: /newsletter/298 returned 200 while the archive listing ended at #297, and both its og:title and <h1> read literally '#298: ...' — a stub, exactly the 2026-08-18 #294 precedent. #297 (processed 2026-09-21) was the densest issue in months: 74 links, headlined by Shopify leaving React Native and Expo SDK 58 beta. #298 expected to go live within days. 2026-09-24: #298 went live (archive listing now shows a real title, 'Astro, Redux, img, Hotkeys, R3F, Next.js, AI, Redact | React…', not the '#298: ...' stub) and was processed — 68 links, 18 pre-dispositioned by prep, 50 judged; 4 keeps (Next.js 16.3.6 security update, Worklets 0.13, R3F 9.8, Shopify Helix). One of its links (Redact 0.1) carries the literal href 'http://releases/' — a broken link in the newsletter itself. Next: probe #299. 2026-10-08: archive listing checked first — #299 and #300 both carry real titles (not '#NNN: ...' stubs) and #301 404s. Processed both: #299 (62 links, 20 pre-dispositioned) kept Preact 11 (RB-E-REACT-CORE) and the Electron-to-PWA reading (RB-E-DESKTOP); #300 (57 links, 15 pre-dispositioned) kept the jjenzz Compiler-context reading (RB-E-STATE) and corrected TesterArmy via its open-source `e2e` framework (RB-E-AI-DEVTOOLS). Prep carried three of this pass's own firsthand keeps as 'previously skipped (other)' because the firsthand rows still read plain `kept` at prep time — corrected in twir-300.md. Next: probe #301 2026-10-15: archive listing checked first — #301 carries a real title (h1 '#301: TanStack Start, React Aria, Base UI…', dated 2026-10-14) and #302 404s. Processed: 71 links, 17 pre-dispositioned (1 by rule), 54 judged, 3 keeps (react-native-web maintained again → RB-E-CROSSPLATFORM; ESLint 10 breaking eslint-plugin-react/import with eslint-config-next's fixupPluginRules shim → RB-E-DX; react-native-nano-icons 1.0 → RB-E-SVG). The blurbs LAGGED THE REGISTRY twice — 'eslint-config-next 16.5 canary' when the shim had shipped in 16.4.0 (2026-10-06, confirmed in the tarball), and 'RN 0.88 at RC5' when rc.6 was out — so version facts come from npm, never from the blurb. Next: probe #302

react-status.name: React Status
react-status.notes: corroboration-heavy; headliners usually already held. Probed FIRST per the standing note: #490 AND #491 were both live on 2026-09-21 and both processed. #490 originated the Tailwind-Labs-joins-Shopify keep; #491 originated the VITE DEV-SERVER CVE keep (CVE-2026-39364) — which sat FAR DOWN its link list and was only caught because the coverage gate demands a row per link. Lesson recorded: this source buries real finds below the headline items, so never triage it from the headlines alone. Next: probe #492 (publishes Thursdays). 2026-09-24 (Thursday): re-probed #492 and #493 — both 404 and the archive listing ends at #491, so nothing new yet; probe again next pass (publishes Thursdays, sometimes late in the day). 2026-10-01: #492 ('Signals come to React-Redux') went live and was processed by the 10-01 pass (39 links, 12 pre-dispositioned, 3 keeps: @tanstack/redact figures corrected, the projecting-react primary source, the vitonsky design-system reading); the state file was not advanced at the time and was corrected 2026-10-08. 2026-10-08 (Thursday): `harvest prep react-status` re-probed at the end of the pass — 'no new issue after #492 (probed 493, 494)'. Next: probe #493 2026-10-15: #493 ('Next.js 16.4, and a new way to visualize React apps', dated 2026-10-09) processed — 44 links, 19 pre-dispositioned, 25 judged, 2 keeps (Coinbase leaving RN via a LinkedIn post → RB-E-CROSSPLATFORM, reopening twir-300's unverifiable row; Remix 3.0 stable → RB-E-META-FRAMEWORKS). Both keeps were BURIED again — Coinbase in IN BRIEF, Remix in 'Elsewhere in the ecosystem' — while the headline (julesblom's visual notation) was off-scope; the judge-every-row rule keeps paying. The editor wrote that they are off next week and back Friday 2026-10-23, so #494 is expected around 2026-10-23, not 10-16. Thursday re-probe 2026-10-15 (end of pass): /issues/494 and /issues/495 404 with the browser UA, archive listing ends at #493; `harvest prep react-status` after the state bump: 'no new issue after #493 (probed 494, 495)'. Next: probe #494 (~2026-10-23)

react-digest.name: React Digest
react-digest.notes: issues slug-titled by featured article; article/depth-driven. Archive: /newsletters or /newsletters.rss (newest-first, resolves the slug) — /digests 404s. Slug numbers are NOT sequential (2344 → 2350 → 2355 → 2360 → 2365). #2365 ('The browser's main thread is expensive', processed 2026-09-21) yielded ZERO keeps — 12 links, half of them sibling-newsletter cross-promotion, and its React items (React 19.3, the Rust compiler post, a React-internals tutorial) were all already held. That is TWO consecutive zero-yield issues (#2360, #2365); if #2370 also yields zero, measure its origination rate the way React Weekly's was measured before deciding whether it earns its slot. 2026-09-24: #2370 ('Write React. Ship direct DOM.', dated 2026-09-20) BROKE the zero-yield streak by originating one keep (the translate-shield browser-translator DOM article, an I18N gap); its Vidact link was a re-sighting of a TWiR #296 lead, not an origination. That resets the zero-yield streak (1 origination in 13 links), so the pre-committed origination-rate measurement is not triggered; revisit only if #2375 and #2380 both yield zero. 2026-10-08 MEASURED: #2375 (2026-09-27, 13 links) yielded ZERO keeps; #2380 (2026-10-04, 13 links) yielded ONE keep — the Marmelab offline/realtime reading (RB-E-DATA), reopened because #2380 was its second independent sighting after React Status #491, so it is a corroborating keep, not an origination. Originations: 0 of 26 links across both issues; 8 of the 26 rows are the publisher's own sibling-newsletter/media-kit chrome. By the letter of the pre-committed rule (keeps) the measurement is not triggered; by originations it would be — flagged for the maintainer in the 2026-10-08 LEDGER rather than decided here. Next: probe #2385 via /newsletters.rss 2026-10-08 RETIRED by the maintainer on the origination measurement: 0 originations in 26 links across #2375/#2380, lifetime 1 origination in the last 5 issues (#2360–#2380), and roughly a third of each issue is the publisher's own sibling-newsletter chrome — do not process further issues; kept in this file with active:false so the ×29 count keeps matching encyclopedia sources_digested and the decision stays visible. Archive is /newsletters.rss, so the backlog stays reachable if this is ever reversed.

react-native-rewind.name: React Native Rewind
react-native-rewind.notes: slug-titled; each issue page carries an authoritative 'Issue #NN' label near the title — use THAT, not sequential guesswork, to resume (verified again 2026-09-21: the two newest slugs labelled themselves #57 and #56). RSS at /newsletter-rss.xml (newest-first) 307-redirects — curl -L; canonical host is www.thereactnativerewind.com. #57 ('React Native is DEAD, Expo Modules 2.0, and a $49 Flutter knockoff') was almost entirely commentary on the Shopify announcement plus Expo Modules 2.0 — both kept from PRIMARY sources, so it originated nothing; its remaining links are background references (UIView, Yoga, Fabric, Impeller). 2026-09-24: #58 ('Uninstalling Cursor, Extreme PR Makeovers, and 33 Percent Less Thread-Blocking JSON', published 2026-09-21; the page labels itself 'Issue #58') originated nothing — 27 links, all already-held, sponsor chrome or too-early tweets; its headline 'LazyJSON' claim lives only in an x.com tweet with no package to verify. 2026-10-08: #59 ('Crease-Proof Layouts, Brain Rot Without the Black Frames, and Un-Breaking a Non-Breaking Release', 2026-09-28, labelled 'Issue #59') and #60 ('Mega Carrots for Monty, Angular Through the Sliding Door, and Lynx on Foldables', 2026-10-05, 'Issue #60') both originated nothing — 22 and 21 links, all already-held, corroboration, pre-ship or chrome. Next: read the RSS head for #61 2026-10-15: #61 ('The Great Graphite Migration, Derek Joins Fat Fighters, and a Leaderboard for Your Dependency Tree', RSS 2026-10-12; page label 'Issue #61' verified) originated nothing — 21 links, all already-held, corroboration, too-early new libs or chrome. Its 'stable 0.88 scheduled for October 12' line did not happen on npm (latest 0.87.1, next 0.88.0-rc.6 on 10-15). `harvest prep react-native-rewind` cannot resolve this source (no url_pattern; slug-titled), so the manifest was hand-built from `harvest inventory <issue-url>`. Next: read the RSS head for #62 2026-10-15b: `harvest prep react-native-rewind` NOW RESOLVES this source — it reads the RSS feed (`feed`) newest-first and takes the issue number off each page's 'Issue #NN' label (`issue_label`), stopping at the last processed issue; the hand-built-manifest path is only the fallback if discovery fails.

native-weekly.name: Native Weekly
native-weekly.notes: nativeweekly.com is a shell — use the beehiiv archive (slugs like /p/sep-11-2026-issue-20). NOTE THE SLUG TYPO TRAP: #21's slug reads 'sep-18-2025-issue-21' (2025, not 2026) — trust the issue number, not the date in the slug. Author also authors rnsec (watch self-promotion). Cadence has tightened to roughly fortnightly: #19 2026-08-28 → #20 2026-09-11 → #21 2026-09-18. Two issues processed 2026-09-21. The standing read holds: its release-roundup rows duplicate the firsthand watch almost entirely (#21 was ~20 npm/GitHub rows, all corroboration) and the ARTICLES are where its keeps are — #20 originated the Margelo-joins-Callstack keep, which no other source this pass carried. 2026-09-24: archive re-checked — nothing after #21 (the /p/ list still ends at the mistyped 'sep-18-2025-issue-21' slug). 2026-10-08: #22 ('Reanimated 4.7, RN 0.88 RC2 & Xcode JSON', slug sep-25-2026-issue-22, datePublished 2026-09-25) processed — 52 links, originated nothing (release roundup + jobs + chrome; its Apex link is now held via Callstack's GA post). Archive /p/ list ends at #22. Next: probe for #23 2026-10-15: archive /p/ list re-checked by hand — still ends at sep-25-2026-issue-22; nothing new (`harvest prep native-weekly` only prints 'check manually' for this source). Next: probe for #23 2026-10-15b: `harvest prep native-weekly` NOW RESOLVES this source — beehiiv has no feed (/feed 404s), so prep scans the archive page for /p/<date>-issue-NN slugs (`archive_slug`) and trusts the NUMBER, never the date in the slug.

react-weekly.name: React Weekly
react-weekly.notes: RETIRED 2026-09-21 — do not process further issues; kept in this file so the ×30 count keeps matching encyclopedia sources_digested and the decision stays visible. The 2026-09-10 criterion was pre-committed precisely so this would not be re-argued from one quiet issue: 'if #37 also originates zero keeps, that is four consecutive and the structural argument is proven: drop it then.' Measured on 2026-09-21: #37 originated ZERO (all six links already-held or corroboration — jotai v3, RN 0.88-rc.0, the Rust-compiler post, Expo Modules 2.0, React 19.3, Expo Go login) and #38 originated ZERO (Shopify back-to-native, the KMP study, Discord New-Arch, SDK 58 — every one of them carried by TWiR #297 or already held). That is issues 34-38, FIVE consecutive with no origination, against a lifetime rate of 9 keeps / 65 rows (14%) across 29-36. The structural reason, now proven rather than suspected: its editorial is a subset of TWiR + the firsthand watch, and the overlap grew as firsthand coverage grew. IRREVERSIBILITY WARNING kept on the record: its RSS window is the latest 20 issues only, so this backlog becomes permanently unreachable (issues 1-7 already are). To resurrect it, re-measure origination over three fresh issues before trusting it again
